government.note: State institutions under the Dayton constitution (Annex 4 of the 1995 Dayton Agreement). The head of state is a three-member Presidency (one Bosniak and one Croat member elected from the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, one Serb member elected from Republika Srpska) with a rotating chair. The Presidency nominates the Chair of the Council of Ministers, who takes office on approval by the House of Representatives; until June 2000 the Council of Ministers had two co-chairmen. The bicameral Parliamentary Assembly has a directly elected House of Representatives (42 members: 28 from the Federation, 14 from Republika Srpska) and a House of Peoples (15 delegates: five Bosniaks, five Croats and five Serbs, chosen by the entity parliaments). An international High Representative oversees civilian implementation of the Dayton Agreement and holds the 'Bonn Powers' to impose legislation and remove officials. The two entities and the Brčko District have their own institutions, which are not modelled as offices here.

name.en: Parliamentary Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina

system.note: 28 members from the Federation (21 in five multi-member units plus seven compensatory seats) and 14 from Republika Srpska (nine in three units plus five compensatory seats), Sainte-Laguë, 3% threshold at entity level (current law). seats_2000 is the result of the October 1998 election; joint lists are recorded under their leading party: the SDA–SBiH–LS–GDS Coalition for Unity and Democracy (17) under SDA, and the Sloga list of SNS, SP and SNSD (4) under SNS. Others: Serbian Radical Party (2), NHI–HKDU (1), Union of Social Democrats (2), Radical Party of Republika Srpska (1) and Democratic People's Union (1). Changes before 1 January 2000 were not checked.

Five Bosniak and five Croat delegates chosen by the Federation's House of Peoples and five Serb delegates chosen by the National Assembly of Republika Srpska. Party composition on 1 January 2000 was not checked, so all 15 seats are recorded as appointed.

source.title: Wikipedia: House of Peoples of Bosnia and Herzegovina

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from the October 1998 House of Representatives vote (shares computed from the vote counts), with joint lists assigned by their leading party: SDA-led Coalition for Unity and Democracy 33.8%, Sloga (SNS–SP–SNSD) 12.4%, SDS 9.4%, Serbian Radical Party 6.9%, Radical Party of Republika Srpska 1.6% and Serbian Coalition for Republika Srpska 1.5% (national conservative); HDZ BiH 11.6% and NHI–HKDU 2.3% (Christian democrat); SDP 9.3% and Union of Social Democrats 1.7% (social democrat); the Democratic People's Union 1.2% and the remaining lists (about 8.3%) as big tent. Voting followed ethnic lines, which this mapping does not capture. ruling_parties lists the parties holding the Presidency seats and the Council of Ministers co-chairmanships in January 2000 (the Council's full party composition was not checked).

source.title: Wikipedia: Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina
